item.title: Data Integration - External APIs
item.description:
Data Integration - Working with External APIs

This week focused on integrating external data sources into the backend system.

The goal was to understand how a backend application can communicate with third-party APIs, consume data, and integrate it into an existing domain model.

Understanding external APIs

Before implementing anything, I spent time understanding how APIs work in practice:

  • HTTP requests (GET, POST)
  • JSON as the standard data format
  • endpoints and query parameters

This was a shift from working purely with internal systems to interacting with external services.

item.title: Backend design - MORE CRUD!
item.description:
Designing the Backend Domain - JPA, Relations, and Queries

This phase of the project has focused entirely on building a solid backend foundation using Java, JPA, Hibernate, and PostgreSQL.

The goal was not to build features quickly, but to design a domain model and persistence layer that:

  • reflects real-world relationships
  • is easy to reason about
  • can be extended safely as new technologies are introduced later in the semester

Domain-driven database design with JPA

Instead of starting with SQL tables, I designed the system around domain concepts, letting JPA handle table creation and relationships.
